strategyReview: The direct Polymarket YES-overpricing edge remains the strongest part of the book: clean ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_NO live sits at 4/4 with +18.42% average trade, the gated upside-barrier cousin is 116/191 shadows with +1.93% average, and the PANEL_NO_7D findings show holdout-confirmed near-dated/mid-priced NO edge. Weekend HL funding reversion still wins per trade (70%) but its weekend-clustered evidence is only marginally positive, while the shadow-mined static-threshold variants are failing. The biggest drags are: static funding triggers that catch worsening funding rather than normalization, one-touch/no-bias edges being scored as spot-direction bets instead of contract premium decay, Polymarket proxy shorts transmitting almost no edge, and the HYPE-confirms-BTC cross-asset family failing. Tonight I allocate five slots to sharpening the NO-edge panel families and five to mechanical refinements of the diagnosed failures, and I am not opening any new proxy or HYPE/BTC confirmation tests.

failureClusters.theme: Static weekend funding triggers without confirmation
failureClusters.evidence: CBRS shadow variant H-539 is 16/34 (47%), AAPL H-537 is 13/27 (48%), and MU H-535 is 8/21 (38%). Losses repeatedly show funding moving from already-negative readings to much more negative values, e.g. CBRS -1.0% to -98.5%, MU 5.5% to -28.6%, and AAPL -5.9% to -17.7%.
failureClusters.recommendation: Do not treat a single raw funding < -10% observation as a reversion trigger. Require weekend scope, a relative extreme within the asset's recent distribution, and evidence that funding has already begun turning higher before taking the long reversion trade.

failureClusters.theme: Contract edge scored as spot prediction
failureClusters.evidence: GOLD no-bias rich-tail H-532 is 53% scorable with 7 burned unscorable tests, and GOLD one-touch heatmap H-534 is 35% scorable with 7 burned unscorable tests. Their wins are recorded as contract P&L, e.g. NO on GOLD above 5000 0.495 to 0.530, while the primary prediction asks for spot declines greater than 2%.
failureClusters.recommendation: Re-author these as contract premium decay trades on above-strike NO positions, not spot-move bets. Stop adding spot-direction tests to what is really a rich-YES premium fade.

failureClusters.theme: Polymarket proxy short shadows without edge
failureClusters.evidence: FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG_PM_PROXY_SHORT is 3/24 (12.5%) with -2.97% avg, PC_RATIO_EXTREME_LOW_PM_PROXY_SHORT is 1/19 (5.3%) with -6.14% avg, and OPT_IV_GT_PM_IV_DOWNSIDE is 2/16 (12.5%) with -9.95% avg.
failureClusters.recommendation: Do not promote proxy shorts. The real edge is selling overpriced Polymarket YES directly; using spot/perp signals as a proxy for buying NO on analogous contracts weakens or inverts the edge.

failureClusters.evidence: cross_asset_iv_compression_vol_expansion is only 9/25 (36%) across many variants. Example losses show BTC falling -3.47% or rising only 0.70% despite HYPE spot above its 24h SMA and stable OI.
failureClusters.recommendation: Treat HYPE spot/OI stability as coincident risk-on behavior, not independent confirmation of durable BTC upside. Freeze this family and reallocate test capacity to the richer NO-edge panel cuts.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-539: the failing trigger was a static CBRS funding reading below -10% on any day. This version requires a true weekend, a recent relative funding extreme, and confirmation that funding has already begun turning higher.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS funding normalizes upward within 2 days from a weekend extreme after it has already begun turning higher.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-537: the failing trigger was a static AAPL funding reading below -10% on any weekday. This version requires weekend scope, a relative extreme, and a current 24h turn higher.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL funding normalizes upward within 2 days from a weekend extreme after it has already begun turning higher.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-535: the failing trigger was a static MU funding reading below -10% without weekend or turning confirmation. This version requires weekend scope, a relative extreme, and a 24h turn higher.
newHypotheses.prediction: MU funding normalizes upward within 2 days from a weekend extreme after it has already begun turning higher.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-532: the failed variant predicted a GOLD spot decline when its actual wins were NO contract price appreciation. This version re-authors the signal as an above-strike GOLD one-touch NO premium fade.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on above-strike GOLD one-touch contracts is profitable over 7 days as NO premium appreciates and YES premium decays.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-534: the failed variant predicted a GOLD spot decline when the trade was actually a rich-YES one-touch NO premium fade. This version restricts to above-strike contracts and re-authors the outcome as contract P&L.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on above-strike GOLD one-touch contracts is profitable over 7 days as YES premium decays or the contract settles NO.

newHypotheses.description: Panel NO edge sharpest cut with a liquidity guard: sub-point sell-YES model edge, mid-priced YES ask, near expiry, and at least one liquid market.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on contracts meeting these conditions is profitable over 7 days as the mid-priced near-dated NO position appreciates.

newHypotheses.description: Panel NO edge above-strike variant with tight spread: above-strike one-touch contracts, mid-priced YES ask, and a tight bid-ask spread.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on above-strike one-touch contracts meeting these conditions is profitable over 7 days as YES premium decays.

newHypotheses.description: Panel NO edge broad mid-price variant with liquidity guard: mid-priced YES contracts with at least one liquid market.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on mid-priced contracts with sufficient liquidity is profitable over 7 days as YES premium decays.

newHypotheses.description: Panel NO edge near-dated mid-price variant with a tighter spread guard than the parent finding.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on near-dated mid-priced contracts with a sub-1c spread is profitable over 7 days as YES premium decays.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The static cbrs_hl_funding_ann < -10 trigger produces roughly coin-flip outcomes because funding can keep falling after entry, e.g. -1.0% to -98.5% and 14.4% to -23.2%. The signal is catching extreme prints, not actual normalization.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A static cbrs_hl_funding_ann below -10% is a sufficient timing trigger for >2% CBRS spot move within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL tests show the same pattern: funding readings below -10% on non-weekend and weekend-like observations frequently continue lower, e.g. 5.5% to 5.5% no normalization and -5.9% to -17.7% deterioration.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: AAPL funding below -10% on any day reliably normalizes and yields a >2% spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: MU funding below -10% produced inconsistent normalization, with 5.5% to -28.6% and post-spike 183.7% to 30.2% losses. The single static threshold is not equivalent to a weekend funding capitulation signal.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A single MU funding reading below -10% reliably normalizes and produces >2% MU spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The scorable tests show the actual P&L is NO contract appreciation, e.g. NO on GOLD above 5000 0.495 to 0.530, while the primary prediction demanded spot declines. Several tests were burned unscorable by this mismatch.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large no-bias adjusted gap on rich GOLD tail NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The one-touch GOLD heatmap signal wins when evaluated on NO contract premium decay, not when predicted as a GOLD spot decline. The spot-move formulation caused a low scorable win rate and burned 7 tests.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large gold underlying-cap edge on upside one-touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% GOLD spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: HYPE spot above its 24h SMA with stable OI did not independently confirm BTC upside. BTC still fell -3.47% in one test and only rose +0.70% in another, leaving the family well below a useful edge on the long-BTC exam.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE spot above its 24h SMA with stable OI independently confirms durable BTC upside rather than late-stage FOMO/overextension.

journalEntry: Tonight's review returns the book to the proven Polymarket YES-overpricing edge. The panel NO evidence is strong and holdout-confirmed, especially in mid-priced, near-dated bands, so five authored hypotheses sharpen that family. Five refinements fix diagnosed mechanical failures: weekend funding reversion now requires weekend scope plus relative extreme plus a turn higher; the two GOLD shadow families are re-authored as contract premium decay trades instead of impossible spot predictions. I made no parameter updates because weekend-clustered live evidence is not statistically positive enough to move the funding entry band, and the one-touch risk is locked.
